item.title: Ralliston's Journey through all of the 001 proposals - Part Two - Scranton's Proposal
item.content:encoded:
Review: I will be honest - the format screw isn't interesting enough to carry the article by itself; unfortunately, there isn't much here other than it. What really makes me dislike it is the fact that the article doesn't really even take advantage of what it tries to do; as a result, it wages its value on a format screw that isn't even exploited enough to be interesting. It just kinda… is there I guess?

Yes, I understand that this was written a long, long time ago, but still; there are some really good articles from that time period. This one, in my opinion, unfortunately, isn't one of them.

Result: -1

item.content:encoded:
"white noise was again heard emanating from the auditorium"

Awkward construction (passive voice). Has the same issue as "this change sees [some effect]…" common in poorly-written news articles. Consider "guards reported white noise emanating" as in the previous paragraph, or a similar structure. "Second incidence of white noise reported on [date]" also possible: still passive voice unfortunately, but in line with tech doc writing styles.

item.content:encoded:
"Sir, how many members of the O5 council are there?" one rookie asked, from the back of the auditorium.
The Senior Agent blinked, before replying, "Twelve."
Murmurs of dissent rippled around the auditorium as the new staff looked at each other in consternation. Wasn't this guy meant to know this off by heart? Hadn't he had over ten years' worth of experience under these very people?
Another dissident stood up from his seat. "Doesn't the booklet say that there are 13 council members?"
"No, it's just that we have an O5-13, that's all. I'll count 'em all for you. O5-1, O5-2, O5-3, O5-4, O5-6, O5-7, all the way to O5-13."
"But, sir, what about the fifth one?"
The Agent stared back at him blankly. "O5…5?"
"Yeah, that one."
"What do you mean, that one? We've never had an O5-5."

item.content:encoded:
I really like this one because it's a non-definitive origin story. While I love the other 001 proposals that are origin stories, they're too… definitive? This one is basically "so this may be how the Foundation started, but we're not really sure what's going on here, so it might not be." I dunno, the idea of the Foundation existing in that maybe/maybe-not space is what makes me enjoy it so much—which is probably why this is my favorite 001 proposal, because it implies that the Foundation is an SCP in and of itself. Which is my favorite idea.

(That, and it simultaneously goes along with my image of O5 being a group of people in ceremonial soft-meat crowns.)

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Thanks. Being new, it's nice to have my over-thinking appreciated. It was one of those half-conscious insights that the light of day tends to make vanish. I just couldn't express the idea (or be certain that it could be expressed). Since you like it, I'm glad I was typing at the time!
I think I was trying to articulate the idea that in some Platonic sense, both are "the SCP Foundation." Trying to disentangle the actions, membership, facilities, and holdings of one from the other might, especially given time to interweave, be impossible. Even if they are equally malevolent/benevolent, mad, and effective, the two Foundations would be differently malevolent, mad, and effective. One could view this as either an infection at the organization's heart, or as a source of hybrid vigor, and people within either facet of the foundation might hold either view.
It reminds me a bit of my reaction to the end of the movie the Thing.

+ (spoilers)
- Title for hiding text

[If you are an exact alien duplicate of yourself, constructed from you own flesh, is that a bad thing? I mean you are out to take over the world - by replacing everyone with alien duplicates - but is that a bad thing? Does defacto equal dejour]

So, would it be a bad thing?
Wait. This is SCP. Yes. Maybe not for the obvious reasons, but it would be unimaginably bad.

item.content:encoded:
This one is full of fun ideas to play with.
So either the Foundation was evacuating (or expanding) from a previous world or something "else" was doing the same and had its imperatives mixed up with the UIU mission. Interesting. I agree with a lot of other people that I really don't like this as an origin, but it would be a good mindfucking piece of misinformation inside the Foundation.
Also, this was the 50s, since then, it is likely that the Foundation and its thralls/agents have gotten better at interacting with the world, when needed.

Oh, and I know this wasn't Scantron's intention, but the article made no statement that SCP didn't exist in that world previously. What if the 001 secret is that when a sort of Bizarro SCP was insinuated into reality, it somehow became inseparable from the real SCP. (I'm not sure if I'm expressing the notion right, and I'm certain it is too weird to fit into most headcanons, including my own) So the secret would be that somewhere within SCP is an extradimensional incursion, and that in a sort of conceptual double exposure … er, never mind, I shouldn't let myself comment while I am a 1am zombie. If someone can get a fun insight, or just a madman's rant out of that, you are welcome to it.

Anyway…good job.
